x-axis in $ relative to new MW, running from -4 to 17+
95% CI error bars (rcap) on each bar
Sharp large negative bar in the bin just below MW (bin -1, ~-0.0135)
Large positive spike at the MW bin (bin 0, ~0.015) of comparable magnitude
Significant positive bar around $3 above MW (bin 3, CI above zero)
Small/statistically insignificant bars in upper-tail bins ($5+)

rationale: The expected file figures/figures/Figure2.pdf exists and, on visual inspection, faithfully reproduces the paper's Figure II event study. It shows light-blue bars of employment change by $1 wage bin on an x-axis from -4 to 17+ ('Wage bins in $ relative to new MW'), each with 95% CI (rcap) error bars, and an overlaid red running cumulative-sum line. The signature pattern is exactly as claimed: a sharp negative spike in the bin just below the MW (bin -1, ~-0.0135), an equal-and-opposite large positive spike at the MW bin (bin 0, ~+0.015), a smaller but CI-above-zero positive bar around $3 above, and small/insignificant bars across the upper tail ($5 and above). The step (plan step 3, 'Figure 2: event-study of employment change...') ran successfully via the R/fixest port of the original Stata do-file (Stata was license-gated; fix_severity.json rates this port 'major' but methodology-preserving), with the log reporting 'E=0.571; per-bin estimates for bins -4..+7'. Two minor cosmetic annotations from the paper are not reproduced: the inset text box with Delta_a/Delta_b and the affected-employment/wage percentages is absent from the plotted PDF, and the running-sum line is solid pink rather than dashed red. These are annotation/style differences, not structural contradictions; all core described visual features match, so the verdict is match.
